property_summary: For any two consecutive calls to airDrop from the same caller, the correct contract always reverts on the second call due to the nonReentrant lock, while the buggy contract succeeds on the second call, leaving a tokenBalance of 40 instead of 20.

After any sequence of calls to airDrop from distinct callers, the correct contract's nonReentrant lock prevents re-entrant double claims, so no single caller's balance ever exceeds 20; the buggy version (lacking the lock) allows a caller to claim twice, resulting in a balance of 40 for some caller.

For any caller who has never called airDrop before, the correct contract always sets the caller's tokenBalance to exactly 20; the buggy contract (without the reentrancy lock) can allow an external Bank contract that re-enters airDrop via supportsToken() to increment the balance beyond 20, violating the invariant that a first-time single airDrop results in balance 20.

For any two distinct addresses that are both eligible (zero balance and correct Bank token support), a successful airDrop by one must not change the tokenBalance of the other; the mutant (without nonReentrant) allows a malicious Bank to re-enter airDrop via supportsToken, causing the first caller's address to receive tokens that are credited to a different target during re-entrancy, thus altering the other address's balance.
For any caller, airDrop must only execute if the caller's tokenBalance is 0; the mutant allows repeated calls, causing tokenBalance to exceed the intended single-drop limit.
For any caller, the total tokenBalance across all addresses after any sequence of airDrop calls never exceeds 20 per caller; the mutant allows repeated calls to the same caller, exceeding this limit.
For any admissible caller, at most one successful airDrop can occur; the bug allows multiple successful calls to the same caller, violating this invariant.

If airDrop completes without revert for a caller, the caller's tokenBalance after the call must equal their balance before plus 20; the mutant allows a second successful call that reverts due to overflow check failure, breaking the invariant for that caller.

For any caller that completes airDrop, the caller's tokenBalance after the call is either exactly 20 or strictly greater than before; the mutant permits a second call for the same caller that succeeds and breaks this post-condition.

For any caller address, after a successful `airDrop`, their `tokenBalance` must be at least 20 more than before; the buggy version can overflow and wrap around, resulting in a balance less than the initial balance plus 20.

For any caller who has zero balance and a bank that supports the token, after a successful airDrop the tokenBalance of the caller equals 20; the buggy version allows an overflow that can leave the balance less than 20 or even zero.

For any two calls to airDrop by distinct callers, the sum of both callers' tokenBalances in the reference remains at most 40, but the buggy version can overflow one caller's balance such that the sum exceeds 40.

For any caller with zero initial balance, the tokenBalance after a successful airDrop is always strictly greater than before the call; the buggy version can overflow and leave the balance equal to the initial balance (0).
After airdrop, any address that was eligible (zero initial balance) will have exactly 20 tokens in the correct contract, but the buggy contract gives 19.
For any caller that successfully calls airDrop, the tokenBalance of the caller increases by exactly 20 in the correct contract, but only by 19 in the buggy contract.
After any successful airdrop, the caller's balance in the correct contract equals 20, while in the buggy contract it equals 19.

After any sequence of calls to airDrop (by any caller), the nonReentrant modifier's lock must return to false in the correct version, allowing further calls, but in the buggy version it remains permanently locked, causing subsequent calls to revert.
After calling airDrop once, the nonReentrant lock in C must be false (allowing a second call to succeed), while in the buggy version the lock remains true causing the second call to revert.
